Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Attached is a consolidated response pack (Redwood_IAM_Detailed_Responses.pdf) and a separate SCIM mapping/spec example (SCIM_Mapping_Spec.yaml). Below are the highlights called out for your security team; the attached PDF contains full answers and references to API endpoints and sample IdP metadata URLs.

Inline summary answers (high level):

Q: SAML support
A: We support SAML 2.0 for both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. SAML metadata URL: https://sso.redwood.ai/saml/metadata. We publish an XML metadata blob and consumable IdP metadata for common providers (Okta, Azure AD, Ping). Certificate rotation is supported via key rollover with RFC-compliant timestamps.

Q: OIDC support
A: We support OIDC (authorization code flow with PKCE) for interactive apps and token introspection for backend integrations. Discovery endpoint: https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/openid-configuration. We support RS256 signed ID tokens and allow configurable token lifetimes per client.

Q: SCIM provisioning
A: We implement SCIM 2.0 (RFC7644) with endpoints for bulk create/update/delete, delta syncs using the since parameter, and support for group membership sync. Deprovisioning is supported via 404 on GET + replace operations; we honor active:false attribute for soft deprovisioning. Rate limits for SCIM are documented in the PDF; we also provide a SCIM mapping YAML (attached) with common AD/Okta attribute examples.

Q: RBAC and delegated admin
A: Our platform provides role-based access control with a default set of admin roles (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Read-only Auditor, Developer, Model Admin). Customers can create custom roles scoped to routes, models, and resource groups. Delegated admin is supported via Org-level roles to assign per-team admins; all role assignments are auditable. Roles support granular CRUD on API keys, model routes, and deployment actions.

Q: Audit logs and retention
A: We retain audit logs for 365 days by default for Dedicated/Private customers; Hosted customers can add retention packages. Logs are exportable via S3 export, syslog drain, and downloadable CSVs through the Console API. Audit events include actor, IP, user-agent, action, resource, and before/after deltas when applicable.

Q: MFA and session controls
A: We defer primary authentication to the customer's IdP for SSO flows (recommended), supporting MFA enforced by the IdP. For account-level fallback, Redwood supports TOTP MFA and configurable session timeouts from 15 minutes up to 30 days for long-lived service accounts.

Q: Admin console controls & emergency access
A: The Console supports just-in-time elevation for sensitive actions (requires approval workflow), IP allowlisting for admin logins, and emergency break-glass keys that are logged and subject to rotation.

Q: SCIM edge cases and performance
A: Delta syncs are efficient and include resourceVersion tokens to resume. For very large directories we support chunked bulk operations and batching; our Dedicated customers typically configure a per-tenant SCIM rate limit to balance performance.

Q: Sample metadata and configuration
A: See attached PDF for sample SAML IdP/Service Provider metadata, OIDC client registration snippet, and example SCIM attribute mappings for displayName, givenName, familyName, userName (email), externalId, and department.

Next steps:

- If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call with one of our security engineers and a solutions engineer to walk through the SCIM mapping and SAML metadata ingestion.
